entries.name: WebVR
entries.definition: A JavaScript API that let web pages show virtual reality content on headsets, since replaced by WebXR.

entries.name: Weed control
entries.definition: Managing or removing unwanted plants in crops, lawns and other land by mechanical, chemical, cultural or biological means.

entries.name: Welding symbols
entries.definition: The standardised symbols on engineering drawings that show the type, size, location and process of each weld.

entries.name: WhatsApp
entries.definition: A mobile messaging and voice and video calling app owned by Meta.

entries.name: Wi-Fi 6
entries.definition: The Wi-Fi Alliance name for the IEEE 802.11ax wireless networking standard.

entries.name: Wi-Fi architecture
entries.definition: The design of Wi-Fi wireless networks, including how access points, controllers, clients and channels are arranged to give coverage and capacity.

entries.name: Wi-Fi Direct
entries.definition: A Wi-Fi Alliance specification that lets devices connect to each other directly over Wi-Fi without a router or access point.

entries.name: Wi-Fi security
entries.definition: Protecting wireless networks and their users, for example with encryption protocols such as WPA2 and WPA3, authentication and access control.

entries.name: Wi-Fi test engineering
entries.definition: Testing Wi-Fi devices and networks for conformance, interoperability and performance.

entries.name: Wide area network
entries.definition: A computer network that links sites across a large geographic area, such as cities or countries.

entries.name: Wildlife observation
entries.definition: Watching and recording wild animals, their behaviour and their numbers in the field.

entries.name: Will and testament preparation
entries.definition: Drafting a will, the legal document that states how a person's property is to be distributed after death.

entries.name: Windows 10
entries.definition: The Microsoft operating system for personal computers released in 2015.

entries.name: Windows 7
entries.definition: The Microsoft operating system for personal computers released in 2009.

entries.name: Windows 8
entries.definition: The Microsoft operating system for personal computers released in 2012, known for its tile-based Start screen.

entries.name: Windows Meeting Space
entries.definition: A Windows Vista feature for sharing programs and documents with other people over a network during a meeting.

entries.name: Windows Performance Analyzer
entries.definition: A Microsoft tool for viewing and analysing event traces to find performance problems in Windows and its software.

entries.name: Windows Performance Recorder
entries.definition: A Microsoft tool for recording event traces of how Windows and its software perform, for later analysis.

entries.name: Windows Performance Toolkit
entries.definition: A set of Microsoft tools for recording and analysing event traces to diagnose performance problems on Windows.

entries.name: Windows software development
entries.definition: Writing software that runs on the Microsoft Windows operating system.

entries.name: Windows software trace preprocessor
entries.definition: A Microsoft preprocessor, part of the Windows Driver Kit, that adds event-tracing code to software such as drivers.

entries.name: Windows support
entries.definition: Helping users with problems on computers that run Microsoft Windows.

entries.name: Windows systems administration
entries.definition: Configuring and operating computers and servers that run Microsoft Windows.

entries.name: Windows Vista
entries.definition: The Microsoft operating system for personal computers released in 2007.

entries.name: Windows Vista startup process
entries.definition: How Windows Vista boots, using the Windows Boot Manager and the boot configuration data store in place of NTLDR and boot.ini.

entries.name: Windows XP Media Center Edition
entries.definition: A version of Windows XP, first released in 2002, with extra features for recording and playing TV, music, photos and video on a home computer.

entries.name: Windows XP Professional x64 Edition
entries.definition: The 64-bit version of Windows XP Professional for x86-64 processors, released in 2005.

entries.name: Wine education
entries.definition: Teaching and learning about wine, including grape varieties, regions, production and tasting.

entries.name: Winemaking
entries.definition: Producing wine, from handling grapes and fermenting the juice to ageing and bottling it.

entries.name: WinJS
entries.definition: A Microsoft JavaScript library of user-interface controls and helpers for building Windows and web apps.

entries.name: Wireless technologies
entries.definition: Technologies that carry data or signals without cables, such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, cellular and radio.

entries.name: WKWebView
entries.definition: An Apple WebKit class for showing web content inside iOS and macOS apps.

entries.name: Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act
entries.definition: A 1998 US federal law requiring group health plans that cover mastectomy to also cover breast reconstruction and related care.
variants: Women'S Health And Cancer Rights Act (WHCRA)

entries.name: Women's studies
entries.definition: The interdisciplinary academic study of women's lives, history and roles in society, and of gender.

entries.name: Word embedding
entries.definition: A natural-language-processing technique that represents words as lists of numbers so that words with similar meanings lie close together.

entries.name: Word formation
entries.definition: The ways new words are made in a language, such as adding prefixes and suffixes, joining words and shortening them.

entries.name: Word processing
entries.definition: Creating, editing and formatting documents with word-processing software.

entries.name: Word VBA
entries.definition: Writing Visual Basic for Applications code to automate tasks and extend Microsoft Word.

entries.name: word2vec
entries.definition: A family of shallow neural-network models, introduced at Google in 2013, that learn word embeddings from large amounts of text.

entries.name: Workers' compensation claims
entries.definition: Handling claims for benefits that employees make after a work-related injury or illness, from filing and investigating to settling them.
